roman/nijmegen-roman-cavalry-face-helmet.geometryReview: Reviewed the exact immutable derivative against the Erfgoed Gelderland / Valkhof Museum source thumbnail and all ten candidate orientations. It retains the complete surviving Roman face helmet: face mask with ears, hinged decorated forehead band and its small busts, extant helmet material and neck guard. The missing upper helmet bowl is the source-documented archaeological loss, not a defect to reconstruct. Variant B, +Y/[0,0,0]/yaw0, places the forehead above the eyes, nose and chin, with the exterior face toward the initial camera. The curved metallic element below/behind the face belongs to the surviving helmet/neck-guard scope; no modern mount enters the measured Y bound. Museum height 24.2 cm is the documented complete-surviving-object measurement, including its extant neck guard. Height binding would give whole X width 25.05 cm, versus the museum width 22.8 cm; this is one documented height-axis calibration and must not be described as complete two-axis agreement. Final scale decision: exact/verified AR stays disabled pending proportion reconciliation. Height calibration Y=0.242 m would imply width 0.250548 m instead of the source 0.228 m, about 9.9% larger; decoded mesh-local extents are a unit cube and preserved source-world proportions do not reconcile this discrepancy.

roman/roman-cavalry-pendant-maastricht-3.geometryReview: Reviewed the exact immutable derivative against the Centre Ceramique Maastricht source thumbnail, the complete ten-view sheet and a supplementary rendered source-front candidate. It retains the suspension loop, two broad side lobes, lower central hanging lobe, irregular archaeological edges, brass/corrosion surface and readable museum inventory writing. The material is double-sided and unlit. Sheet J is upright but exposes the reverse of the scanned face, making inventory writing reversed and swapping the source left/right surface features. Applying a world-Y 180-degree turn to J is exactly equivalent to +Y/modelRotation [90,90,0]/yaw0. The actual supplementary thumbnail confirms this final pose: loop above, hanging lobe below, green corrosion at left and readable inventory writing at upper-right, matching the author source image. No modern support is present. The source explicitly gives approximate 7 × 7 cm only; no exact calibration or verified-size AR eligibility is justified.

scaleRecommendation.note: Source explicitly says approx. 7 × 7 cm (L × W). An approximate display size may be labelled as such, but exact/verified-size eligibility remains disabled.
